hook.line: Google just released their guidelines for showing up in AI. I read the whole thing so you don't have to.
hook.visual: Handheld selfie close-up of a man in a cap outdoors under trees, red-box title 'Googles Guide: Showing up in Ai' at the top; the camera settles after a shaky first second.

beats.what: News hook plus 'I read it so you don't have to', with a red title card on top
Cut; promises three actions for business owners and a bonus, while a 'Save this for later' label shows
Cut to point 1 with a '1. Content strategy' title: what E-E-A-T means
Cut; generic '7 tips' blog versus a unique first-hand angle, Google's own example
Point 2 card 'Google business profile (yes it's still important)': fill it in, post, reply to reviews
Point 3 card 'Site speed & mobile': compress images first
Cut to the promised bonus with a '4. Be in as places as possible' card: directories, review sites, forums
Why: AI search is everywhere, so more mentions paint a clearer picture for AI models
Soft close: hope this helps, ask me questions

why_it_works: 'I read the whole thing so you don't have to' sells saved time and borrows authority from Google as the source
Numbered promise (three things plus a bonus) gives an open loop that holds viewers until the bonus at 86 s
Each point gets a numbered title card at the top, so a viewer joining mid-way knows where they are
Concrete before/after example (a generic '7 tips' post vs a first-hand sewer-line story) makes E-E-A-T actionable, and the 'save this' label drives saves and shares
weaknesses: One 67 s shot in the middle with no cuts, visuals or captions; only the brief title cards break it up
No spoken captions, so muted viewers get only the section titles
Never shows the Google document or an example, so the 'official guide' is taken on trust
Weak ending with no follow or comment ask
for_robert: Copy the numbered-plus-bonus promise and the top title card per point; Fred could hold up each number sign and swim back in with a 'bonus' card at the end to pay off the loop.
